faq.q: What makes a good pademelon name?
faq.a: A good name matches personality, is easy to pronounce, and ideally 1-2 syllables.

faq.q: Should I name based on appearance?
faq.a: Yes! Distinctive features make wonderful naming inspiration.

faq.q: Can I use a human name?
faq.a: Absolutely. Human names are popular and make bonds feel more personal.
Shortlist 3-5 favorites, test them over several days.
Names ending in vowel sounds, especially 'ee', work best for recognition.

faq.q: How do I pick the right name for my Pademelon?
faq.a: Start by observing your Pademelon for a few days — their personality, behaviors, and quirks will guide you toward the perfect name. Say candidate names aloud and notice which ones feel natural. The 'backdoor test' — calling the name from outside — is a reliable measure. Trust your instincts: the name that makes you smile is the right one.

faq.q: What are some unique naming ideas for Pademelons?
faq.a: Look to the Pademelon's natural habitat, distinctive physical features, or behavioral traits for inspiration. Draw from mythology, nature, literature, or your favorite stories. Consider names from languages connected to the animal's geographic origin. The most unique names often come from personal experiences and unexpected sources.

faq.q: Can I change my Pademelon's name if needed?
faq.a: Yes — Pademelons can learn new names at any age. Use the new name consistently with positive reinforcement: treats, affection, and play. Most Pademelons fully adapt within 1-2 weeks. This is common with rescue or rehomed animals who benefit from a name that has no negative associations.
